about: Plain-language summaries of the FOCUS specification's dataset, column and attribute pages, written by Claude (an AI model) from each page at working_draft e9cdcc7.

summaries.specification/attributes/correction_hand: Corrections to previously delivered FOCUS dataset artifacts, whether they update, omit or supplement earlier records, are what CorrectionHandling governs. It exists to keep delivered data consistent over time, protect invoice reconciliation for issued invoices and closed billing periods, and keep changes auditable. It applies to datasets and recognises three correction styles. Under Replacement, which uses the Overwrite delivery mechanism, the dataset must provide a complete snapshot of the affected delivery scope, such as a billing period or a contract, superseding earlier artifacts. Under Delta, which uses Append, the dataset must include additive records within the same delivery scope. Under Ledger, also Append, it must include explicit reversal and re-entry records; a reversal repeats the original record with additive metrics such as cost and quantity carrying the opposite sign. The dataset must document which styles it uses and when each applies, accessible to practitioners. Easy to miss: under Delta or Ledger, an accurate view needs every artifact delivered for the scope.
summaries.specification/attributes/currency_format: Columns that hold currency information follow CurrencyFormat, which keeps currency values consistent to reduce friction for practitioners analysing and reporting on cost data. A currency can be a national currency, such as USD or EUR, or a consumption currency, such as platform credits or normalized billing units. When a value represents a national currency, the column must conform to ISO 4217:2015 and must use its three-letter alphabetic code. When a value does not represent a national currency, the column must not use an ISO 4217:2015 code. Whether a value is a national currency follows from the column's own definition or documentation, not from the format of the value, and a single column can carry both types, for example a national currency on purchase rows and a consumption currency on usage rows. Which currency types a column allows is set by that column's own requirements, not by this attribute.
summaries.specification/attributes/custom_column_h: When the standard FOCUS columns cannot capture everything about a service, data generators may add custom columns, and CustomColumnHandling sets their naming, formatting and value rules. The one mandatory naming rule is that every custom column ID must start with the x_ prefix, marking it as external and avoiding conflicts with FOCUS columns in future releases. After the prefix, the ID should use Pascal case and only alphanumeric characters, should avoid abbreviations other than Id and acronyms other than Sku, should not exceed 50 characters, and should end in Id for identifiers or Name for names. Two value rules are also mandatory: a custom column containing JSON objects must have its object schema documented and accessible to practitioners, and a numeric custom column must contain a single numeric value. Otherwise, custom columns should conform to NullHandling, DateTimeFormat, NumericFormat, StringHandling, CurrencyFormat and UnitFormat where relevant, and to DataGeneratorCalculatedSplitCostAllocationHandling when the data generator supports that allocation. Documentation for a currency column should say how to tell whether a value is a national currency.
summaries.specification/attributes/data_generator_: Some data generators offer split cost allocation for their own services: one charge record in a FOCUS dataset, the origin charge, is split into several allocated charges that show more granular detail, or detail the origin charge does not show, such as unused capacity. DataGeneratorCalculatedSplitCostAllocationHandling sets the column rules that keep such a split consistent, so the origin charge can be derived from its allocated charges. Practitioners use the feature for chargeback and to understand resource usage, and the allocation method is defined and documented by the data generator. A column representing a dimension must match the origin charge's value when present in an allocated charge, and so must a column representing a non-summable metric, such as a unit price. For a summable metric, such as cost or quantity, the values across the allocated charges must add up to the origin charge's value. The distinction matters: summable metrics are divided among allocated charges, while dimensions and non-summable metrics are carried over unchanged.
summaries.specification/attributes/dataset_complet: If useful data exists only in a native dataset, practitioners cannot rely on a FOCUS dataset as their primary source, so DatasetCompleteness requires datasets to carry custom columns for native dataset columns. Every native column must appear as a custom column unless it is listed as an exclusion with justification in publicly available documentation, and only columns unrelated to invoice reconciliation may be excluded. Custom columns needed for invoice reconciliation must be included when the invoice issuer supports payable invoices and FOCUS columns are not sufficient. Every included custom column must be publicly documented with its description, purpose and relationship to native columns. Values must keep native fidelity, with no lossy transformations such as rounding or truncation, and adding custom columns must not alter aggregated summable metrics such as costs and quantities. Datasets should include columns that correlate records with native records, such as native charge identifiers, even when excludable, and should drop custom columns that duplicate FOCUS columns except during a documented transitional period. Columns should be sorted with FOCUS columns alphabetically first, then custom columns alphabetically.
summaries.specification/attributes/dataset_configu: Because datasets from data generators are often massive, DatasetConfiguration lets practitioners tailor a FOCUS dataset's structure and content, removing large, static or irrelevant columns to cut storage costs and processing time. The page cites managing scale, reducing noise for specific workflows, lowering barriers for spreadsheet users, and removing custom x_ columns for cross-provider comparison. It applies to datasets: a FOCUS dataset must be configurable to include only a user-defined selection of columns. It may offer a default column set, and if it does, that default must include all applicable FOCUS columns. Whatever the selection, the dataset must still meet every column-level requirement in the FOCUS schema. The subtle point is that leaving columns out does not relax the rules for the columns kept: if CommitmentDiscountId and ResourceId are excluded, BilledCost and EffectiveCost still reflect commitment discounts correctly, because each included column follows all its requirements, including those that reference columns not in the dataset.
summaries.specification/attributes/datetime_format: Date and time values follow DateTimeFormat so that they are clear, accurate and easy for both humans and systems to interpret. Every conforming column must be expressed in Coordinated Universal Time, to avoid ambiguity across time zones, and must conform to the ISO 8601 standard, as governed by ISO 8601-1:2019. Stricter rules apply when a column represents a specific moment in time: it must use the extended ISO 8601 format with a Coordinated Universal Time offset, written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. Both the date and the time components must be present, separated by the letter T; hours, minutes and seconds must each use two digits; and the value must end with the ISO 8601 Coordinated Universal Time designator Z. Easy to get wrong: a value for a moment in time that omits the time component, is given in a local time zone, or lacks the trailing Z does not meet these requirements.
summaries.specification/attributes/delivery_handli: How a data generator delivers a FOCUS dataset to a customer is the subject of DeliveryHandling, which applies to datasets and recognises two delivery mechanisms that are often combined. With Overwrite, the dataset must provide a complete snapshot for a delivery scope, such as a billing period or a contract, and must supersede all earlier dataset artifacts for that scope; it is simple but lacks inherent auditability. With Append, new records are added and all earlier artifacts must be preserved, with updates and omissions arriving as new entries for net effects or reversals, which supports auditability at higher data volume. Under either mechanism, the dataset must not require practitioners to deduplicate records within or across artifacts. Delivered artifacts should come with corresponding FOCUS Metadata. Documentation must be accessible to practitioners and must state the mechanism used, the conditions for each when more than one is used, and, when metadata is delivered, how artifacts correlate with the FOCUS Metadata Schema object. A common hybrid uses Overwrite for open billing periods and Append for closed ones.
summaries.specification/attributes/focus_column_ha: Naming conventions for the standard FOCUS columns come from FocusColumnHandling, so that column IDs in dataset artifacts are consistent for practitioners and display names suit reports and documentation. A FOCUS column's display name must match its column ID with spaces between words: BillingAccountName becomes Billing Account Name, and BillingAccountId becomes Billing Account ID, with Id written as ID. Column IDs must use Pascal case and only alphanumeric characters, must not include special characters, and must not use abbreviations other than Id. They should not use acronyms other than Sku and should not exceed 50 characters, to suit the column length limits of various data repositories. An identifier column must end in Id, a name column must end in Name, and a column representing the product offering that incurred a charge must include Sku. Any column whose ID ends in Category must, when not null, contain one of the FOCUS-defined allowed values.
summaries.specification/attributes/json_object_for: JsonObjectFormat extends KeyValueFormat to support complex data such as arrays and nested key-value pairs, for cases the simpler format cannot represent, such as several sets of key-value pairs applying to the same charge record. A conforming column must contain a serialized JSON string that is an object or an array as defined by ECMA 404, and must also meet its own column definition, which may restrict the shape or contents. Keys within an object must be unique, and each value must be a number, string, boolean (true or false), array, object or null. Objects should not exceed three levels of nesting. Objects inside an array must be of a consistent type, must be unique, and must not be null or empty, and they too should not exceed three levels of nesting. Note the difference in strength: the nesting limit is only a recommendation, whereas null, empty or duplicate objects in an array break the format.
summaries.specification/attributes/key_value_forma: Key-value pairs, also called name-value, attribute-value or field-value pairs, are often used in place of separate columns when the data would be sparse or has no predetermined keys, which consolidates related information and keeps the schema more consistent. KeyValueFormat sets the rules for columns holding them. A conforming column must be a serialized JSON string consistent with the ECMA 404 definition of an object, so a bare array does not qualify. Keys must be unique within the object. Each value must be a number, a string, a boolean (true or false) or null. Values must not be objects or arrays, which rules out any nesting: a value that contains another object or a list breaks this format even though it is valid JSON.
summaries.specification/attributes/null_handling.m: Records that have no value to present for a column need consistent handling, and NullHandling provides it to reduce friction for practitioners using the data for analysis and reporting. It applies to the columns that conform to it. When a column is defined as nullable, it must use null for absent values. A column containing string values must not fill an absent value with an empty string or a placeholder string such as Not Applicable. A column containing numeric values must not fill an absent value with a placeholder number such as 0. Easy to get wrong: substituting a blank, a label or a zero where no value exists; an absent value in a nullable column must be null, not something that looks like real data.
Numeric columns follow NumericFormat so their values are clear, accurate and easy for humans and systems to interpret. FOCUS does not require a specific precision; the provider determines it, and it should be part of the provider's published data definition. A conforming column must contain a single numeric value written as an integer, decimal or scientific notation, and non-null values must fit an allowed data type and precision: Integer as Short (16-bit), Long (32-bit) or Extended (64-bit or higher), or Decimal as Single, Double or Extended (128-bit or higher). Values must not include mathematical symbols, functions or operators, units of measure, currency symbols, commas or other punctuation, apart from one decimal point where needed. Negative values must use a minus sign, and positive values must not carry a plus sign. Scientific notation must use E notation, mEn, with a minus sign for a negative exponent and no plus sign for a positive one, so 35.2E-7 is valid but 35.2E+7 is not. Thousands separators, as in 3,432,342, are also invalid.
summaries.specification/attributes/string_handling: String values follow StringHandling to support data integrity, interoperability, consistency and reliable analysis and reporting. A conforming column must preserve the original casing and spacing of string values, plus any other consistency factors the data generator or end user specifies. Immutable strings, such as a resource identifier or region identifier, must stay consistent across all billing periods. For mutable strings, such as a resource name or region name, records for periods after a change must show the new value, and records for periods before the change must keep the earlier value, unless the record is a correction to a previously closed billing period, in which case it may show the new value. Columns whose string values are not nullable should not contain empty strings or strings made only of whitespace. Easy to get wrong: altering the case or spacing of values, or carrying a renamed value back into earlier-period records that are not corrections to a closed billing period.
summaries.specification/attributes/unit_format.md: Units of measure in FOCUS dataset columns, covering data size, time, counts and other dimensions, are standardised by UnitFormat. A unit must include at least one base unit. Data size units must use the allowed abbreviations, such as b, B, KB, GiB or EB, in the same form for singular and plural, so TBs and terabyte are invalid; values above 10^18 must use the exabit, exabyte, exbibit or exbibyte abbreviation, and values below one byte must use bit or byte. Time units must use the allowed names from Year down to Microsecond. Count units should use recommended names such as Request, Token or Core, though unlisted count units may be used, and any unlisted base unit should be a capitalized noun. Compound units must join base units with a hyphen and should read singular-then-plural, as in GB-Hours; ratio units must use a slash, as in GB/Hour. Positive-integer unit and denominator quantities may be added, as in 1000 Tokens or Units/2 Weeks. Time units should be the largest whole unit: 1 Year, not 12 Months.
summaries.specification/datasets/billing_period/co: The timestamp when a Billing Period record was first created, that is, the moment the record was instantiated. It supports auditability of the charge and invoice lifecycle by letting a FinOps practitioner distinguish the time of service consumption from the time the financial record was generated. It is a Mandatory dimension in the Billing Period dataset, of type Date/Time, that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. It was introduced in version 1.4.

The exclusive end bound of a billing period in the BillingPeriod dataset. A period whose BillingPeriodStart is 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and whose BillingPeriodEnd is 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes January but not February, because the start is the inclusive start bound and the end is the exclusive end bound. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. It was introduced in version 1.4.

The timestamp of the most recent moment any column value in a BillingPeriod record was created or modified. It helps FinOps practitioners confirm they are working with the current version of a record, particularly when corrections or status changes were applied after the record was first created. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. Its value must be greater than or equal to BillingPeriodCreated. The column was introduced in version 1.4.

The inclusive start bound of a billing period in the Billing Period dataset. Paired with BillingPeriodEnd, the exclusive end bound, it defines what the period covers: a start of 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and an end of 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes January but not February. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements, must not be null and must be the inclusive start bound of the billing period. It was introduced in version 1.4.

The state of a billing period, showing whether its Cost and Usage and Invoice Detail data is preliminary and subject to change, or finalized and ready for formal financial reporting and showback or chargeback. This Mandatory string must not be null and must be Open, meaning the period is active or still being processed and records may be added or revised, or Closed, meaning all anticipated invoices have been issued and the data is finalized. It describes the period identified by BillingPeriodStart and BillingPeriodEnd. It must not become Open after being Closed unless the customer explicitly requests or approves it.

The name of the entity responsible for issuing payable invoices for the resources or services consumed, commonly used in cost analysis and reporting. In the BillingPeriod dataset it is a Mandatory String dimension that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null, and it must represent the entity that issues invoices. The specification's appendix on participating entity identification gives example values across various use case scenarios. The column was introduced in version 1.4.
summaries.specification/datasets/billing_period/da: A supporting dataset that defines the time intervals and statuses of an invoice issuer's billing cycles, which group and present charges on invoices. It helps FinOps practitioners understand how and when they can use CostAndUsage and InvoiceDetail data for formal financial reporting and for showback and chargeback processes. The dataset must include six mandatory columns, none of which allow nulls: BillingPeriodCreated, BillingPeriodEnd, BillingPeriodLastUpdated and BillingPeriodStart, all Date/Time, plus BillingPeriodStatus and InvoiceIssuerName, both String. Its main role is to give context to the CostAndUsage and InvoiceDetail datasets, which it joins to on the BillingPeriodStart and InvoiceIssuerName columns that those datasets also carry. The dataset must also conform to the specification's requirements for correction handling, dataset completeness, dataset configuration and delivery handling. Its FOCUS columns must follow the FOCUS column handling and null handling requirements, and any custom columns must follow the custom column handling requirements. BillingPeriod was introduced in version 1.4.
summaries.specification/datasets/contract_commitme: The currency of a contract commitment, recorded in the ContractCommitment dataset as a String identifier. It must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements, must match the currency used on the invoice generated by the invoice issuer, and must be expressed in a national currency such as USD or EUR. Its feature level is Mandatory and the column allows nulls, but it must not be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Spend".

A JSON object defining which entities a contract commitment covers and what fraction, from 0.0 to 1.0, of an eligible charge's cost and usage applies. This Mandatory column must not be null and must conform to its JSON schema. IsGlobalScope must be true when the commitment applies to all entities, and IsComplexScope must be true when its logic exceeds the schema. Otherwise Inclusions are required. Inclusions and optional Exclusions hold rules comparing a Dimension, which should be a CostAndUsage column, with Values using operators such as In or StartsWith. A wildcard "*" must be the only value when present.

The primary value or advantage received for a contract commitment. This Mandatory string must not be null and must be one of four allowed values: Discount, a reduction in unit price or list rate; Entitlement, the right to use products, features or software tiers that would otherwise be unavailable; Availability, an assurance of resource access and capacity; and Other. The value reflects the benefit received, not the funding mechanism such as a prepaid pool. When a commitment brings several benefits, it should reflect the primary commercial driver. Availability must not be confused with technical fields such as CapacityReservationId.

The highest-level classification of a contract commitment, based on how the commitment is applied to a charge, commonly used to tell apart categories of contract commitments that may need different handling. It is a mandatory String dimension in the ContractCommitment dataset that must not be null and must be one of two allowed values: "Spend", for commitments that require a predetermined amount of spend, and "Usage", for commitments that require a predetermined amount of usage.

The monetary value of a contract commitment, commonly used to monitor progress towards fulfilling contractual commitments that may facilitate discounts for resources or services. It is a Mandatory metric of type Decimal that must conform to the Numeric Format requirements, accepts any valid decimal value and must be denominated in the BillingCurrency. It must not be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Spend" and may be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Usage". It was introduced in version 1.3.

The timestamp at which a ContractCommitment record was first created, which supports auditability of the contract commitment lifecycle. It is a mandatory Date/Time dimension in the ContractCommitment dataset that must conform to the specification's date/time format requirements and must not be null. The value must represent the moment the ContractCommitment record was instantiated.

A self-contained summary of a contract commitment's terms that gives high-level context without requiring additional discovery, covering what the other columns of the Contract Commitment dataset may not sufficiently describe. It is a String that must conform to the specification's string handling requirements, and its maximum length should be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema. The feature level is Mandatory. The column allows nulls, but the value should not be null. It is a dimension column, introduced in version 1.3.

The effective percentage reduction from list price for resources or services covered by a contract commitment, held as a Decimal from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive. It is a mandatory metric that allows nulls: it must not be null when ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory is "Discount" and must be null when it is "Availability". In a tiered contract, each ContractCommitment row must reflect the discount of the single pricing tier it represents. With several contractual layers it should be the net effective discount, one minus contracted over list unit price, so a 20% commitment discount plus a 10% negotiated discount gives 28%, not 30%.

The categorical length of a contract commitment, such as "3 Years", based on the commercial agreement or pricing model. A mandatory String dimension, it must not be null and must follow string handling requirements. It should use a "[Numeric Value] [Unit]" format with a time unit from Minute through Year, and should reflect the offering's standard duration, not a precise count of days or hours. A time-based value must use the largest whole-number unit, so "1 Year", not "12 Months". It may differ from the span between ContractCommitmentPeriodStart and ContractCommitmentPeriodEnd: an exchanged 3-year commitment keeps "3 Years".

The period over which fulfillment of a contract commitment is measured and reset: the window in which usage is aggregated to decide whether commitment obligations have been met. At the end of each interval the ContractCommitmentModel logic applies, either expiring unused capacity (Continuous) or calculating a balance or true-up (Discontinuous). It is a Mandatory String that must not be null and must be one of ten allowed values, from Hourly, Daily and Weekly up to Annual, plus Full Period, Transactional and Custom. Continuous models are typically Hourly, and the value must not be "Full Period" when ContractCommitmentModel is "Continuous".

A service-provider-assigned identifier for a single contract term agreed between a service provider and a customer; contracts can include commitments to a certain amount of spend or usage over an agreed period. This Mandatory string must not be null, must conform to the String Handling requirements and must be unique within the service provider, and it should be a fully-qualified identifier. Each ContractCommitmentId must have one and only one parent ContractId, and it may match that ContractId.

The timestamp when a Contract Commitment record was last updated, which helps FinOps practitioners confirm they are working with the most current version of the record, particularly after corrections or status changes applied since it was created. It must represent the most recent moment at which any column value of the record was created or modified, and it must be greater than or equal to ContractCommitmentCreated. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null.

The current lifecycle state of a contract commitment, which determines whether the commitment applies to a given period of CostAndUsage data. It is a Mandatory String that must not be null and must be one of seven allowed values: Proposed (being negotiated or modeled, with no legal or financial impact), Pending (finalized or signed, with a future start date), Active (in effect with remaining value), Exhausted (in effect but fully consumed), Expired, Canceled and Superseded. When a record is modified in a way that requires a new ContractCommitmentId, the previous record's status must be "Superseded".

The operational behavior and consumption flexibility of a contract commitment. It is a Mandatory String that must not be null and must be one of two allowed values. "Continuous" is a flat, constant floor of commitment, such as reserved instances or savings plans, applied at a fixed rate per fulfillment interval (usually hourly) with no carry-over, so any dip in usage is unrecoverable waste. "Discontinuous" is a flexible, aggregate commitment, such as an enterprise agreement or software-as-a-service minimum spend, measured over a broad window or against a total monetary value. It must be "Discontinuous" when ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval is "Full Period".

Whether a contract commitment's pricing and terms come from a standard, publicly accessible offering or were brokered through private negotiation. A Mandatory String, it must not be null and must be one of two allowed values: "Public", for terms generally available to all customers through a service provider's standard rate card or portal, or "Negotiated", for terms and pricing modified by agreement between customer and service provider. The page suggests Public as a market-comparison baseline and Negotiated for tracking procurement discounts, noting Negotiated records often fall under non-disclosure agreements, so the field can support data masking or access control.

How often a contract commitment is invoiced: the ongoing billing cycle for payment models with deferred financial obligations, or the single settlement event for upfront models. It is a Mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must be one of the allowed values One-Time, Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual or Custom, for hourly, daily or other irregular cycles. It must be "One-Time" when ContractCommitmentPaymentModel is "All Upfront" and should represent a time granularity equal to or less than ContractCommitmentDurationType's. It differs from ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval: a spend-based commitment discount may have an Hourly fulfillment interval but a Monthly payment interval.

The financial settlement structure of a contract commitment: a single upfront payment, recurring charges, or both. It is a String, must not be null, and must be one of three allowed values: No Upfront (settled entirely through deferred payments, typically recurring charges, with no initial payment), Partial Upfront (an initial payment plus deferred payments) and All Upfront (a single payment at the start of the duration). The feature level is Mandatory. For the upfront cash event the page points to the Contract Commitment Period Start, and for the frequency of recurring payments to the Contract Commitment Payment Interval.

The share of the total Contract Commitment Cost paid at the start of a contract commitment's duration, which allows FinOps practitioners and accounting professionals precise financial modeling of Partial Upfront payment models, separating immediate cash outlays from deferred liabilities. It is a Decimal that must not be null and must be a value between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive. It must be 1.0 when ContractCommitmentPaymentModel is "All Upfront", 0.0 when it is "No Upfront", and greater than 0.0 but less than 1.0 when it is "Partial Upfront". The feature level is Conditional, under the operating model condition Includes Partial Upfront Payments.

The end of a contract commitment period, recorded as the exclusive end bound of the commitment's effective period: the period runs up to but does not include this moment, while Contract Commitment Period Start is the inclusive start bound. For example, a period from 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z includes January 1 2024. It is a Date/Time that must conform to the specification's date/time format requirements and must not be null. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the Contract Commitment dataset, introduced in version 1.3.

The moment a contract commitment's effective period begins, given as its inclusive start bound. With ContractCommitmentPeriodEnd as the exclusive end bound, a start of 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and an end of 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z gives a period that includes January 1 2024. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension in the Contract Commitment dataset that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. It was introduced in version 1.3.

The amount associated with a contract commitment, denominated in the service-provider-defined ContractCommitmentUnit and commonly used to monitor progress toward fulfilling contractual commitments that may facilitate discounts for resources or services. It is a mandatory Decimal metric that must conform to numeric format requirements and can be any valid decimal value. Its nullability depends on ContractCommitmentCategory: it must not be null when the category is "Usage" and may be null when it is "Spend".

A service-provider-assigned name for the type of a contract commitment, commonly used to display and aggregate the kinds of commitments a practitioner has made, stated in the provider's own terms. It is a readable display name, not a code. This Mandatory string must not be null, must conform to the String Handling requirements and must be a consistent, readable display value. It was introduced in version 1.3.

The service-provider-specified measurement unit for the amount declared in ContractCommitmentQuantity, complementing that metric. It is a String that must conform to string handling requirements and should conform to the specification's unit format. Its nullability follows the quantity: it must be null when ContractCommitmentQuantity is null and must not be null when ContractCommitmentQuantity is not null. The feature level is Mandatory, and the column allows nulls. It is a dimension in the Contract Commitment dataset, introduced in version 1.3.

A service-provider-assigned identifier for a contract describing the agreed terms between a service provider and a customer; contracts can include a commitment to a certain amount of spend or usage over an agreed period of time. In the Contract Commitment dataset it is a Mandatory String dimension that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. It must be a unique identifier within the service provider and should be a fully-qualified identifier. It was introduced in version 1.3.

The exclusive end bound of a contract period, that is, of the effective period of the contract itself. The period covers times before this value but not the value itself, while Contract Period Start is the inclusive start bound; a period from 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z, for example, includes January 1 2024. It is a Date/Time that must conform to date/time format requirements and must not be null. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the Contract Commitment dataset, introduced in version 1.3.

The date and time a contract's effective period begins, expressed as its inclusive start bound and recorded in the Contract Commitment dataset. With ContractPeriodEnd as the exclusive end bound, a start of 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and an end of 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z gives a period that includes January 1 2024. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. It was introduced in version 1.3.

The name of the entity responsible for issuing payable invoices for a contract commitment, commonly used for cost analysis, reconciliation and reporting. In the ContractCommitment dataset it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null, must conform to string handling requirements and must represent the entity that issues invoices. No specific value format is defined.

The currency denomination, national or consumption, in which a contract commitment and its ContractCommitmentCost were priced, commonly relevant when a commitment is negotiated in one currency but billed in another. It is a Conditional String in the ContractCommitment dataset, applying under the Includes Pricing-Billing Currency Differences operating model condition. It must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements, must not be null, and must represent a national currency or a consumption currency. Documentation for the column must specify how to determine whether a value represents a national currency and must be accessible to practitioners.

The monetary value of a contract commitment expressed in PricingCurrency, used to track progress toward contractual milestones at the original negotiated value regardless of exchange rate fluctuations. It is a Conditional Decimal metric in the ContractCommitment dataset, applying under the Includes Pricing-Billing Currency Differences operating model condition; it must conform to the Numeric Format requirements, accepts any valid decimal value, and must be denominated in PricingCurrency. It must not be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Spend" and PricingCurrency is provided, and it may be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Usage".

Names the entity that provides the resources or services available for usage or purchase and is responsible for fulfilling a contract commitment's terms, such as applying discounts, managing credit pools or guaranteeing resource availability. In marketplace scenarios it is the seller of the commitment rather than the marketplace operator, unless the operator provides the commitment benefit. It is the reseller when the commitment is made directly with a reseller for white-labeled services, and otherwise the entity that produced the underlying services. A mandatory String dimension, it must not be null and must follow string handling requirements.

Contract terms agreed between a service provider and a customer are the subject of this supporting dataset, introduced in version 1.3. Its 30 columns include the contract and commitment identifiers, ContractId and ContractCommitmentId; contract and commitment periods; commitment cost, quantity, unit and discount percentage; commitment category, benefit category, offer category and duration type; payment model, interval and upfront percentage; lifecycle status; applicability rules; billing currency; and the invoice issuer and service provider names. The dataset must include 27 of these columns in every case. The other three are conditional: ContractCommitmentPaymentUpfrontPercentage must be included when the operating model includes partial upfront payments, and PricingCurrency and PricingCurrencyContractCommitmentCost must be included when the operating model includes pricing and billing currency differences. It joins to the Cost and Usage dataset through ContractCommitmentId, which is a column here but, in Cost and Usage, a property inside the JSON object array held in the ContractApplied column. The dataset must also conform to the shared requirements for correction handling, dataset completeness, dataset configuration and delivery handling, and its specification-defined and custom columns must conform to the column handling and null handling requirements.
summaries.specification/datasets/cost_and_usage/co: A JSON object, serialized as a String where necessary, describing how resources are allocated when usage records are split in a data generator-calculated split cost allocation. It is Recommended, under the Includes Split Cost Allocation operating model condition, and must be null when a charge is not related to such a split but should not be null when it is. Its Elements array holds entries with a required AllocatedRatio, the allocated charge's share of the origin charge, plus an optional UsageQuantity and a UsageUnit, required with UsageQuantity. Ratios across one origin charge's allocated charges must sum to 1.

The identifier of the allocated method, defined by the service provider, that was used for a data generator-calculated split cost allocation; it lets users find in the provider's documentation how an allocated charge was calculated. It is a Conditional string, tied to operating models that include split cost allocation, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when a charge is not related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation and must not be null when it is. The documentation for each such allocation method must reference a single AllocatedMethodId value.

An identifier, assigned by the data generator, for the object to which cost is allocated in a data generator-calculated split cost allocation, used when that target is something other than the charge's ResourceId, as with allocated charges. It is a String. It must be null when a charge is unrelated to such an allocation or represents the unallocated portion of the origin charge, and must not be null on the allocated portion. When present it should be locally unique within the associated ResourceId and ChargePeriod, but may not be unique across them. The feature level is Conditional.

The display name of the object to which cost is allocated in data generator-calculated split cost allocation. It shows what cost is being allocated to in charges where the service provider allocates costs to something other than the charge's ResourceId, as with allocated charges. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes split cost allocation, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when AllocatedResourceId is null and must not be null when AllocatedResourceId is not null. It may duplicate AllocatedResourceId when a separate display name is not applicable.

The display name of the service to which cost is allocated in a data generator-calculated split cost allocation, identifying the consuming service on allocated charges. On those rows ServiceName keeps the origin charge's service, so this column gives the consuming service its own queryable field without overwriting ServiceName. A Conditional String dimension under the Includes Split Cost Allocation operating model condition, it must follow string handling requirements. It must be null when AllocatedMethodId is null and must not be null otherwise, and it should match the ServiceName the data generator uses for the equivalent service.

The tags that apply specifically to allocated charges from a data generator-calculated split cost allocation. It is a JSON object, serialized as a String where necessary, in the key-value format. It must be null when a charge is unrelated to such an allocation and may be null otherwise. When present it must not repeat resource tags already in Tags, must include all applicable user-defined and data generator-defined tags for the AllocatedResourceId, and must give valueless tag keys the boolean value true. Data generator-defined keys must carry a prefix unique to each tag scheme. The feature level is Conditional.

A host-provider-assigned identifier for a physically separated and isolated area within a Region that provides high availability and fault tolerance. It is commonly used to analyze cross-zone data transfer usage and its cost based on where resources are deployed. It is a String that must conform to string handling requirements, and it must be null when a charge is not specific to an availability zone. The feature level is Recommended, under the operating model condition Includes Availability Zones. It is a dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset, introduced in version 0.5.

The cost of a charge as invoiced by the invoice issuer in a billing period, used for invoice reconciliation, cash-based forecasting, budgeting and cost allocation. A Mandatory Decimal in BillingCurrency, it must not be null, must reflect all applicable discounts, and must show invoiced, not estimated, amounts. It must exclude covered-charge portions offset by covering charges and be 0 for fully covered charges, so it can differ from EffectiveCost. It must be 0 for charges from entities not responsible for invoicing. For issued invoices, its sum per InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName must match the payable amount within the Rounding Variance Tolerance.

The identifier an invoice issuer assigns to a billing account, commonly used for grouping by organizational constructs, invoice reconciliation and cost allocation. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. It must be a unique identifier within an invoice issuer and should be a fully-qualified identifier. It was introduced in version 0.5.

The display name assigned to a billing account; billing accounts are commonly used to group by organizational constructs, reconcile invoices and allocate costs. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements. The column allows nulls, but it must not be null when the invoice issuer supports assigning a display name to the billing account. The specification's appendix on grouping constructs for resources or services gives details and examples.

A readable display name, not a code, that the invoice issuer assigns to identify the type of billing account. It is commonly used to map FOCUS and provider constructs, summarize costs across providers, or support invoicing and chargeback. It is a String that must be a consistent, readable display value. It must be null when BillingAccountId is null and must not be null when BillingAccountId is not null. The feature level is Conditional, under the operating model condition Includes Multiple Billing Account Types. It is a dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset, introduced in version 1.2.

The currency a charge was billed in, commonly used when costs need to be grouped or aggregated. It is a Mandatory string that must not be null and must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements. It must match the currency used in the invoice generated by the invoice issuer, and it must be expressed in a national currency, such as US dollars (USD) or euros (EUR). It has been part of the specification since version 0.5.

In the Cost and Usage dataset, this is the exclusive end bound of a billing period. With a BillingPeriodStart of 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and a BillingPeriodEnd of 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z, the period includes charges for January but not charges for February, because the start is the inclusive start bound and the end is the exclusive end bound. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. It dates from version 0.5.

The inclusive start bound of a billing period. A period whose BillingPeriodStart is 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and whose BillingPeriodEnd is 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes charges for January but not February, because BillingPeriodEnd is the exclusive end bound. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements, must not be null, and must be the inclusive start bound of the billing period.

The identifier a service provider assigns to a capacity reservation, commonly used to allocate charges for capacity reservation usage. It is a Conditional String dimension in CostAndUsage, applying under the Includes Capacity Reservations operating model condition, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when a charge is not related to a capacity reservation, must not be null when a charge represents the unused portion of one, and should not be null whenever a charge is related to one. When present, it must be unique within the service provider and should be fully qualified.

Whether a charge represents consumption of the capacity reservation identified in CapacityReservationId or the unused portion of that reservation. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes capacity reservations, with two allowed values, "Used" and "Unused". It must be null when CapacityReservationId is null, and must not be null when CapacityReservationId is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage". When present it must be "Unused" for a charge representing the unused portion of a capacity reservation and "Used" for a charge representing the used portion.

The highest-level classification of a charge based on how it is billed. A Mandatory String dimension, it must not be null and must be one of five allowed values, each covering positive or negative amounts including refunds: "Usage" for consumption, "Purchase" for acquiring a service, resource or commitment, "Tax" for levied taxes, "Credit" for incentives or allowances unrelated to other charges, and "Adjustment" for billing modifications fitting no other category. For "Usage" and "Purchase" charges with a non-null SkuPriceId, it must match SkuPrice.ChargeCategory for the same SkuPriceId and ServiceProviderName, a rule excluded from conformance while SkuPrice is a preview.

A marker showing whether a charge is a correction to a previously closed billing period, separating those corrections from all other charges, including regular charges and corrections to open billing periods. It is a String whose only allowed value is "Correction", covering cases such as refunds and credit modifications. It must be null when the charge is not a correction to a previously closed billing period and must not be null when it is. The feature level is Mandatory, and the column allows nulls. It is a dimension introduced in version 1.0.

A self-contained summary of a charge's purpose and price that gives high-level context for a row without further discovery, typically covering a select group of details from across a billing dataset or information not otherwise available. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements. Although Mandatory, it allows nulls: the rule is only that it should not be null. Its maximum length should be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema.

How often a charge occurs, used with the charge period columns to understand recurrence, forecast upcoming charges and tell one-time from recurring purchase fees. It is a Recommended String dimension that must not be null and must be one of three allowed values: "One-Time" for charges that happen once and will not repeat, "Recurring" for charges that repeat on a periodic cadence whether or not the service was used, and "Usage-Based" for charges that repeat every time the service is used and are not recorded when it is not. It must not be "Usage-Based" when ChargeCategory is "Purchase".

The exclusive end bound of a charge's effective period. With ChargePeriodStart at 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and ChargePeriodEnd at 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z, the period includes charges for January 1 but not January 2, because the start is the inclusive bound and the end is the exclusive one. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null.

The inclusive start bound of a charge period, paired with ChargePeriodEnd as the exclusive end bound. A period starting 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and ending 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z therefore includes charges for January 1 but not for January 2. It is a mandatory Date/Time dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to date/time format requirements, must not be null, and must be the inclusive start bound of the charge's effective period.

Whether the commitment discount identified in CommitmentDiscountId is based on usage quantity or on cost, also called spend. It applies only to commitment discounts, not to negotiated discounts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include commitment discounts, must be one of two allowed values: Spend, for commitment discounts that require a predetermined amount of spend, or Usage, for those that require a predetermined amount of usage. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null and must not be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null.

The identifier a service provider assigns to a commitment discount, used for chargeback and savings per commitment discount; it does not apply to negotiated discounts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include commitment discounts, must be null when a charge is not related to a commitment discount and must not be null when it is. When present, it must be unique within the service provider and should be fully qualified. It must equal ResourceId when ChargeCategory is "Purchase" and the charge purchases that commitment discount, and when ChargeCategory is "Usage" and the charge is its unused portion.

The display name assigned to a commitment discount, applicable only to commitment discounts and not to negotiated discounts. It is a Conditional String dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset under the Includes Commitment Discounts operating model condition, and must follow string handling requirements. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null. When CommitmentDiscountId is not null, it must not be null if a display name can be assigned to the commitment discount, and may be null if one cannot. No specific value format is defined.

The amount of a commitment discount purchased or accounted for, denominated in CommitmentDiscountUnit. It is a Decimal. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null; on "Usage" or "Purchase" rows with a CommitmentDiscountId it must not be null unless ChargeClass is "Correction", when it may be null; otherwise it must be null. On purchases it is the eligible quantity over the term or per charge period, depending on ChargeFrequency; on usage it is the quantity consumed or left unused, depending on CommitmentDiscountStatus. The page advises excluding purchases from utilization totals to avoid double counting. The feature level is Conditional.

Whether a charge consumes part of the commitment discount identified in CommitmentDiscountId or represents the unused portion of the committed amount; it does not apply to negotiated discounts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include commitment discounts, must be one of two allowed values: Used, when the charge utilizes a specific amount of the commitment discount, or Unused, when the charge represents its unused portion. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null, and it must not be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage".

A service-provider-assigned name for the type of commitment discount applied to a row, relevant only to commitment discounts and not to negotiated discounts. It is a Conditional String dimension under the Includes Commitment Discounts operating model condition and must follow string handling requirements. Its nullability mirrors CommitmentDiscountId: it must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null and must not be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null. The specification defines no allowed values or value format, so the provider supplies the names.

The service-provider-specified unit in which a service provider measures the CommitmentDiscountQuantity of a commitment discount; it applies only to commitment discounts, not negotiated discounts. A Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes commitment discounts, it must conform to the String Handling requirements and should conform to the Unit Format requirements. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountQuantity is null and must not be null otherwise. When present it must stay consistent over time for a given CommitmentDiscountId and must represent the unit used to measure the commitment discount, and should reflect commitment discount flexibility when that is accounted for.

The commitment programs that could cover a charge, including commitment discounts and capacity reservations a service provider treats as commitments; it supplies the denominator for commitment coverage metrics. A Conditional JSON object under the Includes Commitment Programs condition, it must not be null for eligible charges, even if no commitment was applied. It must list every eligible public program, may add eligible negotiated programs not broadly applicable across the catalog, and must not reflect temporary restrictions such as quotas or include commitment periods or payment options. Its CommitmentPrograms array of ProgramType entries must include one matching any non-null CommitmentDiscountType.

The volume of a metered SKU used by a resource or service, measured in the Consumed Unit; it focuses on consumption, not pricing, and is often finer-grained than Pricing Quantity. It is a Decimal. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null, when ChargeCategory is not "Usage", or when CommitmentDiscountStatus is "Unused"; on other usage rows it must not be null unless ChargeClass is "Correction", when it may be null. A row whose SkuPriceDetails lacks TokenCacheAction "Read" or "Write" must not include tokens counted on a row that has one. The feature level is Conditional.

The service-provider-specified unit in which a service provider measures usage of a metered stock keeping unit (SKU) associated with a resource or service, complementing ConsumedQuantity. It focuses on consumption rather than pricing and cost, and is often at a finer granularity or over a different time interval than PricingUnit. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes usage measurement, that must conform to the String Handling requirements and should conform to the Unit Format requirements. It must be null when ConsumedQuantity is null and must not be null when ConsumedQuantity is not null.

A JSON object, serialized as a string where necessary, that links a charge to one or more contract commitments to track progress against agreed commitments. This Conditional column, tied to operating models that include contract commitments, must not be null when one or more contract commitments are applied to the charge. Its required Elements array holds objects with ContractId, ContractCommitmentId and at least one of ContractCommitmentAppliedCost, denominated in BillingCurrency, or ContractCommitmentAppliedQuantity, which then needs ContractCommitmentAppliedUnit. ContractCommitmentId must match ResourceId for a purchase of that commitment or its unused portion. Custom keys must start with "x_".

Cost of a charge under negotiated pricing terms, before any discount-bearing commitment programs apply. This Mandatory Decimal must not be null and must be denominated in the BillingCurrency. It must equal ContractedUnitPrice multiplied by PricingQuantity when both are not null, and for usage and purchase charges that are not corrections it must equal ListCost when no negotiated pricing terms apply. It must equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Credit" and be calculated from the related charges' ContractedCost when ChargeCategory is "Tax". For savings aggregation, exclude covered charges on a billed basis or covering charges on an accrual basis.

The negotiated unit price per PricingUnit for the SKU price that SkuPriceId identifies, before any discount-bearing commitment program applies, in BillingCurrency. A Conditional Decimal metric under the Includes Unit Pricing operating model condition, it must be non-negative and must equal ListUnitPrice when no negotiated pricing terms apply. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", must not be null when SkuPriceId is not null or for "Usage" and "Purchase" charges whose ChargeClass is not "Correction", and may be null otherwise. Negotiated discounts appear in it, commitment discounts only in EffectiveCost. Values should not be aggregated.

An identifier for the credential presented on the request that produced a charge, used to tell apart charges that share a principal but were authenticated with different credentials; descriptive attributes belong in Requester Details. It is a String. It must be null when a charge has no associated credential or the credential has no published identifier, and must not be null when it has one. When present it must be unique within the service provider, and must not contain a credential value that authenticates a request, such as an access token or password. The feature level is Conditional.

The cost of a charge based on the resources used, services used or contract commitments recognized in its charge period, reflecting all applicable pricing adjustments, including discounts. It is a Mandatory, non-null Decimal in BillingCurrency. It must equal BilledCost for uncovered usage, for purchases that neither cover nor are covered by other charges, and for taxes and credits; it may differ for adjustments. Covered charges must include their applied share of a covering purchase's BilledCost, and the purchase's own value must be 0. Charges from entities that do not originate the data must be 0, to avoid double counting.

The name of the entity providing the underlying infrastructure on which the service provider's resources or services are deployed, sometimes the service provider itself. A Mandatory String dimension, it must conform to the String Handling requirements. It may be null when the ServiceName involves no underlying infrastructure, such as professional services or software licenses, or when the host cannot be uniquely determined, as for "Tax" or "Adjustment" charges; otherwise it must not be null. It must name the host provider when the customer explicitly selects it or the service provider exposes it, and must match ServiceProviderName in all other cases.

The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier of the Invoice Detail record that encapsulates charges in a billing period for a billing account, letting practitioners map invoice line items to granular charge data for reconciliation and audit. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include payable invoices, must be null when a charge is associated with neither an invoice nor a pre-generated provisional invoice, and must not be null when it is associated with an issued invoice or a pre-generated provisional invoice. It may be generated before an invoice is issued, and it must uniquely identify a record within a given InvoiceId.

The invoice issuer's identifier for the invoice encapsulating charges in a billing period for a given billing account, used for tracking billing transactions and invoice reconciliation. A Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes payable invoices, it must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when the charge is associated with neither an invoice nor a pre-generated provisional invoice, and must not be null otherwise. It may be generated before the invoice is issued, and must be associated with the related charge and BillingAccountId when a pre-generated or provisional invoice exists.

Name of the entity responsible for issuing payable invoices for the resources or services consumed, commonly used in cost analysis and reporting. In the CostAndUsage dataset it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null, must follow string handling requirements and must represent the entity that issues invoices. No specific value format is defined; the specification's appendix on participating entity identification gives example values across different use case scenarios.

Cost of a charge at the service-provider-suggested pricing, before any negotiated pricing terms or discount-bearing commitment programs apply. This Mandatory Decimal must not be null and must be denominated in the BillingCurrency. For non-correction usage and purchase charges, it must reflect neither negotiated pricing terms nor commitment program effects. It must equal ListUnitPrice multiplied by PricingQuantity when both are not null, must equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Credit", and must be calculated from the related charges' ListCost when ChargeCategory is "Tax". For savings aggregation, exclude covered charges on a billed basis or covering charges on an accrual basis.

The service-provider-suggested unit price per PricingUnit for the price identified by SkuPriceId, before negotiated pricing terms or discount-bearing commitment programs, and commonly the starting point for negotiation. A Conditional Decimal metric, applying when the operating model includes unit pricing, it must be non-negative and denominated in BillingCurrency. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", and must not be null when SkuPriceId is not null or when a "Usage" or "Purchase" charge has a ChargeClass other than "Correction". It does not reflect negotiated tiers or negotiated exchange rates, and should be read per row, not summed.

The pricing model applied to a charge at the time of use or purchase, useful for separating list-price from reduced-price charges and spotting chances to raise commitment discount coverage. A Conditional String under the Includes Multiple Pricing Categories condition, it must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", must not be null for "Usage" or "Purchase" charges whose ChargeClass is not "Correction", and may be null otherwise. Allowed values are "Standard" (the billing account's agreed rate, including commitment discount purchases), "Committed" (reduced by an existing commitment discount), "Dynamic" (provider-determined rates that may change) and "Other".

The national or consumption currency in which a resource or service was priced, commonly used where pricing and billing are in different currencies. In the CostAndUsage dataset it is a Conditional String dimension, applying under the Includes Pricing-Billing Currency Differences operating model condition, that must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements and must not be null. It must represent a national currency or a consumption currency, and documentation for the column must specify how to determine whether a value represents a national currency and must be accessible to practitioners.

The negotiated unit price per Pricing Unit for the SKU Price identified by SkuPriceId, in PricingCurrency, before any currency exchange rate conversion or discount-bearing commitment program. It is a non-negative Decimal. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", and must not be null when SkuPriceId is not null or on "Usage" and "Purchase" rows that are not corrections. It must reflect negotiated non-foreign-exchange pricing terms, must not reflect commitment-dependent price effects, and must equal PricingCurrencyListUnitPrice when no such terms apply. Values should not be aggregated into totals. The feature level is Conditional.

EffectiveCost expressed in the PricingCurrency, with the same pricing adjustments, amortizations and exclusions but before any exchange rate conversion to the BillingCurrency. It gives a uniform baseline before converting from a consumption currency, such as platform credits, to a national currency, or from one national currency to another, and supports accrual-based reporting, forecasting and cost allocation. This Conditional Decimal must not be null and must be denominated in the PricingCurrency. It must be included when the operating model includes a consumption currency, and should be included when it includes pricing and billing currency differences.

The service-provider-suggested unit price per Pricing Unit for the SKU Price identified by SkuPriceId, in PricingCurrency, before any negotiated pricing terms or discount-bearing commitment programs such as commitment discounts; it is commonly used for negotiation and rate optimization. It is a non-negative Decimal. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", and must not be null when SkuPriceId is not null or on non-correction "Usage" and "Purchase" rows. It must not reflect negotiated pricing terms or commitment-dependent price effects. Values should not be aggregated into totals. The feature level is Conditional.

The volume of a stock keeping unit (SKU) used or purchased for a resource or service, based on the PricingUnit. Unlike ConsumedQuantity, it focuses on pricing and cost rather than consumption. A Mandatory Decimal metric in Numeric Format, it must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", must not be null for "Usage" or "Purchase" charges whose ChargeClass is not "Correction", and may be null otherwise. When aggregating per SkuId for a SKU with both covering and covered charges, exclude covered charges on a billed basis or covering charges on an accrual basis to avoid double counting.

The service-provider-specified measurement unit for determining unit prices, showing how the provider rates measured usage and purchase quantities after pricing rules such as block pricing, for example Hours, GB-Hours or 1000 Requests. It complements PricingQuantity and, unlike ConsumedUnit, concerns pricing rather than consumption, often at a coarser granularity. Though Mandatory, it allows nulls: it must be null when PricingQuantity is null and must not be null otherwise. This String should follow unit format requirements and, when present, must be semantically equal to the pricing unit in the provider's published price list, and on the invoice where one appears.

An identifier for the principal to which access to a resource or service is granted, used to report and audit cost by principal; its descriptive attributes sit in RequesterDetails. It is a Conditional String dimension under the Includes Requester Attribution operating model condition. It must be null when a charge has no principal or the principal has no published identifier, and must not be null when it has one. When present it must reference a principal and be unique within the service provider, and must not contain a value that authenticates a request, such as an access token or password.

A host-provider-assigned identifier for the isolated geographic area where a resource is provisioned or a service is provided, commonly used to analyze cost and unit prices by where resources are deployed. It is a Conditional string, tied to operating models that include regions, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must not be null when a resource or service is operated in or managed from a distinct region, and it may be null when it is not.

The host-provider-assigned display name of the isolated geographic area where a resource is provisioned or a service is provided, commonly used to analyze cost and unit prices by where resources are deployed. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include regions, must conform to the String Handling requirements. Its nullability follows RegionId: it must be null when RegionId is null and must not be null when RegionId is not null.

A JSON array, serialized as a String where necessary, of key-value entries carrying readable attributes such as Type, Name and Email for the requester behind a charge, while PrincipalId and CredentialId remain opaque keys. Its Principal and Credential entries describe the principal and credential those IDs identify; custom entries cover other levels. It is a Conditional dimension under the Includes Requester Attribution operating model condition. It must not be null when either ID is not null and may be null when both are null. An entry must not appear when its ID is null, and entry keys must be unique.

The identifier a service provider assigns to a resource, commonly used for cost reporting, analysis and allocation. It is a Conditional String dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset, applying under the Includes Provisioned Resources operating model condition, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when a charge is not related to a resource and must not be null when it is. When present, it must be unique within the service provider, should be a fully qualified identifier, and, when CommitmentDiscountStatus is "Used", must identify the resource that received the commitment discount.

The display name assigned to a resource, commonly used for cost analysis, reporting and allocation. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes provisioned resources, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when ResourceId is null or the resource has no assigned display name, and must not be null when ResourceId is not null and the resource has an assigned display name. It must not duplicate ResourceId when the resource is not provisioned interactively or only has a system-generated ResourceId.

The kind of resource a charge applies to, such as Virtual Machine, Data Warehouse or Load Balancer, commonly used to identify cost changes in groups of similar resources. It is a Conditional String dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset, under both the Includes Provisioned Resources and Includes Resource Type Assignment operating model conditions, and must follow string handling requirements. It must be null when ResourceId is null and must not be null when ResourceId is not null. No allowed values or value format are defined.

The highest-level classification of a service by its core function, used for analyzing costs across service providers and tracking workload migration across fundamentally different architectures; each service should have one and only one category, the one that best aligns with its primary purpose. It is a Mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must be one of nineteen allowed values, among them Compute, Storage, Databases, Networking, Analytics, Security and Identity, with Other for new or emerging services that do not align with an existing category.

The display name of the service offering purchased from a service provider, such as a cloud virtual machine, a software-as-a-service database or professional services from a systems integrator; one service can include several kinds of charges, such as compute, storage and networking. Commonly used to analyze aggregate cost trends and filter data to investigate anomalies, it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must follow string handling requirements. Each ServiceName must have exactly one ServiceCategory that best fits its primary purpose, or "Other" when none fits, and should likewise have one ServiceSubcategory, or "Other".

Name of the entity that provides the resources or services available for usage or purchase, whether they are built on a host provider's infrastructure, offered as fully integrated solutions, or complementary offerings such as support, licensing or consulting. In marketplace scenarios it is the seller, not the marketplace operator; when a reseller sells white-labeled resources or services, it is the reseller; otherwise it is the entity that produced them. This Mandatory string must not be null and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It was introduced in version 1.3 to replace the removed ProviderName column.

A secondary classification within a service's ServiceCategory, based on the service's core function, used with ServiceCategory to analyze spend and usage for specific workload types across service providers and to track workload migration between fundamentally different architectures. It is a Recommended String dimension that must not be null and must be one of the allowed values, each with exactly one parent ServiceCategory. Examples include Virtual Machines and Containers under Compute, Relational Databases under Databases, and Generative AI under AI and Machine Learning. Every category has an "Other" subcategory, such as "Other (Compute)", and "Other (Other)" covers services outside every category.

The service provider's unique identifier for a specific stock keeping unit (SKU), a quantifiable good or service offering with specific functionality and technical specifications that can be sold at different price points. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes unit pricing. It must be null for "Tax" charges and must not be null for "Usage" and "Purchase" charges whose ChargeClass is not "Correction". For a given ServiceProviderName and SKU it must stay consistent across billing accounts, contracts, PricingCategory values and any other price factors that do not affect functionality. It may match SkuPriceId.

A description of the functionality a particular SKU meters or measures in a charge. Providers often have several SKUs per service, such as separate object storage, data transfer and encryption SKUs for one storage service, so this shows what each SKU is metering. Examples are Compute Usage, Block Volume Usage, Data Transfer and API Requests. It is a String. It must be null when SkuId is null and should not be null when SkuId is not null, and it should remain consistent over time for a given ServiceProviderName and SkuId. The feature level is Conditional.

Key-value properties describing a SkuPriceId: qualitative and quantitative traits of the stock keeping unit (SKU) plus stable pricing properties such as periods and tiers. Dynamic or negotiable elements like unit prices, currency, effective dates and negotiated discounts are excluded, so charges sharing a SkuPriceId should share the same details. A Conditional JSON object under the Includes Unit Pricing condition, it must be null when SkuPriceId is null and may be null otherwise. Custom keys must begin with "x_", numeric values must represent a single PricingUnit, and applicable FOCUS-defined properties such as CoreCount, ModelId and TokenDirection should be included.

The service provider's identifier for one SKU Price of a resource or service used or purchased, referencing that price in the provider's price list. It must stay consistent over time and across billing accounts or contracts, which supports tracking unit price changes, and each pricing tier gets its own SkuPriceId. A Conditional String under the Includes Unit Pricing condition, it must be null when ChargeCategory is "Tax", must not be null for "Usage" or "Purchase" charges whose ChargeClass is not "Correction", and may be null otherwise. Each value must have exactly one parent SkuId and one PricingUnit per ServiceProviderName.

The service provider's identifier for a sub account, a grouping of resources or services often used to manage access, cost or both; it is commonly used for grouping by organizational constructs, access management and cost allocation. It is a Conditional String dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset, applying when the operating model includes sub accounts, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when a charge is not related to a sub account and must not be null when a charge is related to one.

A sub account's display name, where a sub account is a grouping of resources or services often used to manage access, cost or both. It supports grouping by organizational constructs, access management needs and cost allocation strategies. It is a Conditional String dimension under the Includes Sub Accounts operating model condition and must follow string handling requirements. It must be null when SubAccountId is null and must not be null when SubAccountId is not null. An appendix describes the grouping constructs FOCUS supports.

The type of a sub account, given as a service-provider-assigned readable display name rather than a code. It is commonly used to map FOCUS and service provider constructs, summarize costs across service providers, or support invoicing and chargeback. It is a Conditional String dimension under the Includes Multiple Sub Account Types operating model condition, must follow string handling requirements and must be a consistent, readable display value. It must be null when SubAccountId is null and must not be null when SubAccountId is not null.

The set of tags assigned to tag sources, used to add business context for allocating charges. A Conditional dimension, applying when the operating model includes tags, it holds a JSON object that must conform to the Key-Value Format requirements and may be null. When present it must include all user-defined and provider-defined tags but only finalized ones, with one value selected per key; valueless keys must be set to true. Provider-defined keys must carry a provider-specified prefix unique to their tag scheme, while user-defined keys must not carry a scheme prefix when only one user-defined tag scheme exists.
