summaries.specification/datasets/cost_and_usage/da: The primary FOCUS dataset, describing the cost and usage incurred through using or purchasing a service provider's resources or services. Its columns are dimensions, qualitative values such as dates and resource or service provider information used to categorize and filter, and metrics, numeric values used for aggregation. Some columns must always be present, among them BilledCost, EffectiveCost, ListCost, ContractedCost, BillingAccountId, BillingCurrency, ChargeCategory, ChargePeriodStart, ChargePeriodEnd, ServiceName and ServiceProviderName; others must or should be included when the operating model includes a relevant feature, such as commitment discounts, split cost allocation, regions or tags. It joins to the Contract Commitment dataset through Contract Commitment ID, which is a column there and a property inside the JSON object array in ContractApplied here. The dataset must include charges for unused portions of a commitment, and separate discounted and non-discounted charges when a discount covers only part of a charge; discounts should be reflected in the charges they pertain to, not as separate offsetting charges. Under split cost allocation, the method must be documented and accessible to practitioners, and allocation should be offered on an opt-in basis. The page notes the data may carry personal data, most commonly in RequesterDetails and Tags.
summaries.specification/datasets/invoice_detail/co: Cost of a charge as invoiced by the invoice issuer in a billing period, in the BillingCurrency, used for invoice reconciliation, cash-based forecasting, budgeting and cost allocation. This Mandatory Decimal must not be null, must reflect all applicable pricing adjustments, must exclude any covered portion offset by a covering charge, and must be 0 for fully covered charges. When InvoiceIssueStatus is "Issued", its sum per InvoiceDetailId, InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName must equal the invoice's payable amount. Sums compared with CostAndUsage.BilledCost must stay within the rounding variance tolerance, except when InvoiceIssueStatus is "Open" or, in the invoice-level comparison, ChargeCategory is "Tax".

An invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for a billing account; billing accounts are commonly used for grouping by organizational constructs, invoice reconciliation and cost allocation strategies. In the InvoiceDetail dataset it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null, must follow string handling requirements and must be unique within an invoice issuer. It should be a fully qualified identifier. No specific value format is defined, and an appendix describes the grouping constructs FOCUS supports.

The currency in which a charge was billed, commonly used when costs need to be grouped or aggregated. In the Invoice Detail dataset it is a Mandatory String dimension that must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements and must not be null. It must match the currency used in the invoice generated by the invoice issuer and must be expressed in a national currency. It was introduced in version 1.4.

Within the Invoice Detail dataset, the exclusive end bound of a billing period: a period from 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes January's charges but not February's, because BillingPeriodStart is the inclusive start bound. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. For a given InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName, it must match CostAndUsage.BillingPeriodEnd for the same CostAndUsage.InvoiceId and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName.

Start of the billing period in the Invoice Detail dataset, given as an inclusive start bound. With BillingPeriodEnd as the exclusive end bound, a start of 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and an end of 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes charges for January but not February. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. For a given InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName it must match CostAndUsage.BillingPeriodStart for the same CostAndUsage.InvoiceId and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName.

The highest-level classification of a charge by how it is billed, used to distinguish charge types that may need different handling. In the InvoiceDetail dataset it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must be one of five allowed values, each covering positive or negative charges: Usage, Purchase, Tax, Credit and Adjustment. A charge that does not aggregate several classifications must take the value matching its nature, such as "Tax" for taxes levied by authorities. Unlike the strict per-row categorization in CostAndUsage, an invoice line aggregating several allowed values other than "Tax" may be "Usage".

The moment an InvoiceDetail record was first instantiated, which supports auditing of the charge and invoice lifecycle by separating when a service was consumed from when its financial record was generated. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. When the matching BillingPeriod record's BillingPeriodStatus is "Closed", InvoiceDetailCreated for a given BillingPeriodStart and InvoiceIssuerName must be earlier than or equal to that record's BillingPeriodLastUpdated.

The invoice issuer's description of an invoice line item, giving context for the charge as it appears on the invoice and often summarizing the service, resource or period the line covers, to help with human-readable reconciliation. It is a String that must describe the charges represented by the InvoiceDetailId. The feature level is Mandatory; the column allows nulls, but the value should not be null. Its maximum length should be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4.

Key-value pairs defining the granularity of an invoice line item, used instead of separate columns because the grain varies within one invoice and across invoice issuers, and supporting reconciliation and cost allocation. It is a JSON object, serialized as a String where necessary. It must not be null when one or more properties uniquely define the line's granularity, and must contain all such properties. It should use FOCUS-defined properties where applicable, such as Service Name, Resource ID and SKU ID, whose keys must match the specified spelling and casing; other keys must begin with "x_". The feature level is Mandatory.

The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for an InvoiceDetail record, which encapsulates charges in the corresponding billing period for a given billing account. It lets FinOps practitioners map specific invoice line items to granular charge data, supporting detailed reconciliation and auditability. It is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must follow string handling requirements. It must uniquely identify a record within a given InvoiceId.

The timestamp when an Invoice Detail record was last updated: the most recent moment when any column value of the record identified by InvoiceDetailId was created or modified. It helps practitioners confirm they are working with the current version after corrections or status changes. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null, and it must be greater than or equal to InvoiceDetailCreated.

The identifier an invoice issuer assigns to an invoice that gathers the charges in a billing period for a given billing account. Invoices are commonly used to track billing transactions, support payment processes and reconcile charges against billing periods. In the InvoiceDetail dataset it is a Mandatory String dimension that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. It must uniquely identify the invoice as provided by the invoice issuer, and it may be generated before the invoice is issued.

The date the invoice issuer issued an invoice, serving as the official point of record for the billing document, the start of payment terms, and a reference point for financial audits and period closing. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension in the InvoiceDetail dataset that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements. The column may be null, and it must represent the official date of issuance for the corresponding InvoiceId.

The name of the entity responsible for issuing payable invoices for the resources or services consumed, commonly used in cost analysis and reporting. It is a String that must conform to string handling requirements, must not be null, and must represent the entity that issues invoices. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4, and the specification's appendix gives example values across different use case scenarios.

The publication state of an invoice, which also signals how reliable its delivered CostAndUsage and InvoiceDetail data is. It is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null, must reflect the invoice's current state and must be one of three allowed values: "Open", provisional and subject to change; "Issued", formally issued as a valid financial obligation with finalized data; or "Voided", previously issued but retracted, and not a valid obligation. The status must not return to "Open" after "Issued" unless the customer explicitly requests or approves it, for example to reopen an invoice for corrections.

The currency in which the invoice issuer requires settlement, which is the currency of the financial obligation the invoice creates. It may differ from the Billing Currency and from the currency of the payer's funds or bank account, and it lets practitioners track settlement obligations and foreign exchange impacts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include billing and payment currency differences, must not be null, must represent the currency in which the invoice payment was made or is expected to be made, and must be a national currency such as US dollars (USD) or euros (EUR).

BilledCost expressed in the PaymentCurrency, used to reconcile financial records in the currency of actual settlement when it differs from the billing currency. This Conditional Decimal, tied to operating models that include billing and payment currency differences, must not be null and must be denominated in the PaymentCurrency. Its grain may differ from BilledCost: it may be non-zero while BilledCost is 0 when it aggregates amounts stated in other records, and it may be 0 while BilledCost is non-zero when that amount is represented in a separate aggregate record. The page's examples link such records through PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId.

A reference to the InvoiceDetailId of the record where the current row's PaymentCurrencyBilledCost is aggregated, linking granular records to aggregate records stated in the currency chosen for settlement so that reconciliation works across different grains. It is a Conditional String dimension under the Includes Aggregation Level Currency Differences operating model condition; it must not be null and must follow string handling requirements. It must match the InvoiceDetailId of the record holding that aggregation, and when PaymentCurrencyBilledCost is non-zero it must match the current record's own InvoiceDetailId.

The deadline by which the invoice issuer expects to receive payment for an invoice, used by FinOps practitioners and finance teams to manage cash flow, prioritize payments and avoid late fees or service interruptions. It is a Date/Time that must conform to date/time format requirements and must be the date the invoice issuer specifies as the payment deadline for the corresponding InvoiceId. It may be null. The feature level is Mandatory, and the column allows nulls. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4.

The terms, typically focused on timeframe, under which the invoice issuer expects to receive payment for an invoice, such as "Net 30". They define the agreed period for settling the invoice, helping the provider and the customer manage financial expectations and payment schedules. It is a String that must conform to string handling requirements, must not be null, and must represent the payment terms as defined on the corresponding invoice. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4.

The unique customer-issued identifier for tracking the lifecycle of a purchase, typically given to the invoice issuer so that charges map to the customer's internal procurement records or purchase orders. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include purchase order numbers, must conform to the String Handling requirements and may be null. It must represent the identifier the customer uses to uniquely identify the purchase order responsible for the charge.

An invoice-issuer-assigned identifier that links an invoice affecting charges stated on a previous invoice back to that original invoice, typically for credits, refunds or corrections, giving direct lineage between adjustments and the original billing records. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. It must match the InvoiceId of the original invoice when the invoice adjusts another, and must match the current invoice's own InvoiceId when it does not, rather than being null.
summaries.specification/datasets/invoice_detail/da: A transactional dataset recording charges as they appear on invoices from an invoice issuer, so FinOps practitioners can perform financial reconciliation, tax reporting and payment processing. Where the CostAndUsage dataset gives granular visibility into consumption, InvoiceDetail keeps alignment with the physical or electronic billing documents. It must represent every invoice line item with a non-zero BilledCost on any invoice associated with a BillingAccountId, and its documentation must say how records correspond to invoice line items and whether line items with a BilledCost of 0 are excluded. Required columns include BilledCost, BillingAccountId, BillingCurrency, ChargeCategory, BillingPeriodStart and BillingPeriodEnd, InvoiceId, InvoiceDetailId, InvoiceIssueDate, InvoiceIssueStatus, InvoiceIssuerName, PaymentDueDate, PaymentTerms and ReferenceInvoiceId. PaymentCurrency, PaymentCurrencyBilledCost, PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId and PurchaseOrderNumber are required only under specific operating model conditions, and custom columns must capture any invoice monetary metric with no FOCUS column equivalent. The dataset joins to CostAndUsage on InvoiceIssuerName and InvoiceId, optionally with InvoiceDetailId, though one or both need aggregating before comparison. Some data generators populate these keys in CostAndUsage while the billing period is open, others only after it closes and invoices are issued. It was introduced in version 1.4.
summaries.specification/datasets/sku_price/columns: The highest-level classification of a stock keeping unit (SKU) price by what is being priced, separating published rates for consumption-based usage, published fees for upfront or recurring purchases, and published unit values for granted credits. It is a Mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must be one of three allowed values, "Usage", "Purchase" or "Credit". Unlike the Cost and Usage column of the same name, it has no "Tax" or "Adjustment" values by design, because service providers do not publish SKU prices for them. It was introduced as a preview in version 1.5.

The basis of the commitment discount a SkuPrice record relates to: usage quantity or cost, also called spend. It applies only to commitment discounts, not negotiated discounts. A Conditional String under the Includes Commitment Discounts condition, introduced as a preview in version 1.5, it must be "Spend", for discounts requiring a predetermined amount of spend, or "Usage", for those requiring a predetermined amount of usage. It must not be null when the record represents a commitment discount purchase or a usage rate that applies under one, and must be null otherwise.

A service-provider-assigned identifier for a contract with a customer; a null value marks a public list price not tied to a contract. The Contract Commitment dataset holds the contract's terms. It is a String. It must be null when the record is not contract-specific or UnitPriceType is "List", and must not be null when it is contract-specific or UnitPriceType is "Base" or "Contracted". When present it must be unique within the service provider and should be fully qualified. Only SkuPriceEligibility determines which entities are eligible for the price. The feature level is Mandatory; introduced as a 1.5 preview.

The currency a resource or service is priced in, which may be a national currency or a consumption currency, regardless of the currency it is ultimately billed in. It is a String that must conform to string handling and currency format requirements, must not be null, and must represent a national currency or a consumption currency. Its documentation must be accessible to practitioners and must specify how to determine whether a value represents a national currency. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the SKU Price dataset, introduced as a preview in version 1.5.

Whether a SkuPrice record's PricingCurrency is a national currency the customer can pay in or a consumption currency issued by the service provider. It is a Mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must be one of two allowed values: "Payable" when PricingCurrency represents a national currency, and "Consumable" when it represents a consumption currency, such as platform credits. Multiplying usage by a "Payable" rate gives a base financial cost, needing currency conversion only if the billed currency differs, while a "Consumable" rate gives a virtual cost balance that requires a secondary conversion to reach the financial cost.

A service-provider-assigned identifier for the geographic area where a price in the SkuPrice dataset applies, used to join rates to actual usage. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include regions, must represent the provider's own regional construct, even a global or macro-region. It must not be null when the price is specific to a distinct region and may be null when it applies globally or is not regionally scoped. Unlike RegionId, it marks where the rate is valid, not where a resource is provisioned. A null or "global" value cannot reliably separate worldwide from non-regionalized scope.

Display name of the service under which a price in the SkuPrice dataset is published in the service provider's price list, used to compare unit prices across services or filter price lists. This Mandatory string must not be null, must conform to the String Handling requirements and must represent the service offering the provider defines for the price, even when it groups several distinct underlying services. It can differ from ServiceName in Cost and Usage, which names the service of the actual usage; those ServiceName values can instead be captured as inclusion criteria in SkuPriceEligibility.

The service-provider-specified measurement unit in which an offering's unit price is defined, such as Hours, GB-Months or 1,000,000 Tokens. Unlike the Consumed Unit in Cost and Usage data, it follows the provider's rate card and is often coarser than raw usage measurement. It is a String that should conform to the unit format and must not be null. When a record prices a currency, PricingUnit must match a PricingCurrency value of records whose PricingCurrencyCategory is "Consumable". It differs from PricingCurrency: a token is a unit of processing, not a currency. The feature level is Mandatory; introduced as a 1.5 preview.

The categorical length of a purchase's term, such as "1 Year" or "3 Years", based on the commercial agreement or pricing model; for a commitment discount, it is that discount's term. As a stable classifier, a three-year term exchanged after a few months stays "3 Years". A Conditional String under the Includes Purchases condition, and a preview in version 1.5, it must be null when ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Credit" and may be null for "Purchase". It should be a positive integer then a time unit such as Week or Years, matching the offering's standard duration rather than exact days or hours.

The settlement structure of a purchase: one upfront payment, recurring charges, or both over the PurchaseDurationType; for a commitment discount it describes that commitment discount's settlement. It is a Conditional String dimension in the SkuPrice dataset under the Includes Purchases operating model condition, introduced as a preview in version 1.5. It must be null when ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Credit", must not be null when it is "Purchase", and must be one of "No Upfront", "Partial Upfront" or "All Upfront". Each payment model offered is published as a separate SKU price record, even at the same price.

The inclusive upper boundary of a quantity-based pricing tier for a SkuPrice record, measured in its PricingUnit. With QuantityTierMinimum, the exclusive lower bound, it defines the quantity range for a unit price: a quantity is in the tier when it is greater than the minimum and no more than the maximum. A Conditional Decimal metric, applying when the operating model includes quantity tier pricing, it must be null when the tier has no upper limit, as for the highest tier or a flat rate, must not be null when a higher tier exists, and must be strictly greater than QuantityTierMinimum.

The exclusive lower boundary of a quantity-based pricing tier for a SKU Price, measured in the PricingUnit: the unit price applies to quantities above this threshold. Together with Quantity Tier Maximum it defines the exact quantity range for a unit price, and for flat-rate or non-tiered pricing it is typically zero. It is a non-negative Decimal that must not be null. The feature level is Conditional, under the operating model condition Includes Quantity Tier Pricing. It is a metric in the SKU Price dataset, introduced as a preview in version 1.5.

The name of the entity providing the resources or services to which a SKU Price applies, including complementary offerings such as support, licensing or consulting. It is commonly used to filter rate cards by vendor or compare providers' prices. In marketplace scenarios it is the seller, not the marketplace operator; for a reseller selling white-labeled resources or services it is the reseller; otherwise it is the entity that produced them. It is a Mandatory String in the SkuPrice dataset, introduced as a preview in version 1.5, that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null.

A service-provider-specified unique identifier for a stock keeping unit (SKU): a quantifiable good or service offering with specific functionality and technical specifications, such as a per-user subscription seat or consulting hours. Each SkuId can carry several SKU Prices varying by tier, commitment period or negotiated terms. It is the primary identifier for looking up a SKU in a provider's catalog or price list and for joining rate card data with usage. A Mandatory String in SkuPrice, it must not be null and must stay consistent across contracts and any factors that affect price but not functionality.

The timestamp at which a SKU Price record was first created, meaning the moment the record was instantiated. It supports auditing of the rate card publication lifecycle by letting practitioners distinguish when the provider generated a pricing record from when it becomes effective, which SKU Price Effective Start records. It is a Date/Time that must conform to date/time format requirements and must not be null. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the SKU Price dataset, introduced as a preview in version 1.5.

A self-contained, high-level summary of a SKU Price's purpose, offering and unit price that gives context without further discovery. It typically covers a select group of details found elsewhere in the SkuPrice dataset or provides information not otherwise available. It is a Mandatory String dimension, introduced as a preview in version 1.5, that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. Its maximum length should be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema.

The exclusive date and time from which a SkuPrice record is no longer active; with SkuPriceEffectiveStart it defines the validity window of a rate card entry. This Mandatory Date/Time column must be null when the price has no upper time boundary, including a price published ahead of taking effect, and must not be null when it has a designated end. A null does not mean the price is currently in effect. It must be greater than SkuPriceEffectiveStart when both are not null. A charge falls under the price when its ChargePeriodStart is before this value or the value is null.

The inclusive date and time from which a SkuPrice record applies to a given SkuPriceId, reflecting when the price becomes contractually or publicly applicable rather than when a practitioner first uses the SKU. A CostAndUsage charge falls under the price when its ChargePeriodStart is on or after this value, and with SkuPriceEffectiveEnd it defines a rate card entry's validity window. A Mandatory Date/Time dimension introduced as a preview in version 1.5, it must be null when the record has no lower time boundary and must not be null when it has a designated start; a null means unbounded, not unknown.

A JSON object of inclusion and exclusion rules stating which entities, accounts or contexts are eligible for a SkuPrice record. A Mandatory dimension, it must not be null and must conform to the JSON Object Format and SkuPriceEligibilityObject requirements. IsGlobalScope must be true when eligibility is not restricted to an enumerated set of entities, like a standard public list price, and IsComplexScope must be true when the logic exceeds schema capabilities. Each rule names a Dimension, which should be a Cost and Usage column, an operator such as In or Exists, and Values, where the wildcard "*" must appear alone.

A service-provider-specified unique identifier for a specific stock keeping unit (SKU) price, the primary reference key for that price in a provider's price list. A mandatory String dimension introduced as a preview in version 1.5, it must not be null. Each SkuPriceId must have exactly one parent SkuId, PricingUnit and ChargeCategory, and, where quantity tier pricing applies, one QuantityTierMinimum and one QuantityTierMaximum, which can be null. It must stay consistent over time and across contracts or billing agreements, as dynamic and negotiable properties such as unit price and currency are excluded from it. It may match SkuId.

When a SkuPrice record was last updated: the most recent moment any of its column values was created or modified, helping FinOps practitioners confirm they hold the current version of a rate card record after corrections or metadata updates. It is a mandatory Date/Time dimension, introduced as a preview in version 1.5, that must follow date/time format requirements, must not be null and must be greater than or equal to SkuPriceCreated. It may be later than SkuPriceEffectiveEnd, because corrections can be applied to a retired rate, so price history should be rebuilt from SkuPriceEffectiveStart and SkuPriceEffectiveEnd rather than audit timestamps.

The service-provider-published price for a single Pricing Unit of the associated SKU Price, in the PricingCurrency. When Contract ID is null it is the standard public price; when populated it is specific to that contract, and Unit Price Type shows which kind, for example a "Base" list price fixed for the contract or a "Contracted" rate. It is a non-negative Decimal that must not be null, and values should only be viewed in the context of their row, not aggregated. The feature level is Mandatory. It was introduced as a preview in version 1.5.

The category of rate held in UnitPrice, distinguishing a standard public price, a contract baseline, a negotiated price or a provider-specific type. A mandatory String dimension introduced as a preview in version 1.5, it must not be null. It should use the recommended values "List" for a price not specific to a contract, "Base" for a list unit price fixed for a ContractId at a point in time, and "Contracted" for a contracted unit price for a ContractId, and may use provider-specific values when none fits. It must not be "Base" or "Contracted" unless the record fits that meaning.
summaries.specification/datasets/sku_price/dataset: The primary dataset for standardizing a service provider's catalog rates, multipliers and negotiated prices, letting practitioners perform precise rate lookups, analyze commitment discounts and understand how payable and consumable prices work. It describes the full price list a provider offers as of the date it is captured, not only the stock keeping units (SKUs) that appear in Cost and Usage, and is not derived from Cost and Usage data; a provider may partition delivery, for example by region. It must use the Overwrite delivery mechanism and should contain at least one record for every SkuPriceId referenced in Cost and Usage. It must not contain two records with identical values, including nulls, across ServiceProviderName, SkuPriceId, ContractId, SkuPriceEffectiveStart, PricingCurrency and UnitPriceType, nor overlapping effective periods for records sharing the other five. It joins to Cost and Usage through SkuPriceId in a one-to-many relationship, so resolving a charge's price also means matching ServiceProviderName, effective period, contract, pricing currency and a single UnitPriceType; it can optionally join to Contract Commitment on ContractId. SkuPrice is a preview in version 1.5: its columns, requirements and relationships may change, its requirements are not evaluated for conformance, and neither is the Data Model requirement to include it.
